timepoint: Over the course of the study
notes: 52 serious adverse events in 42 (4%) of 963 participants; no deaths; per-arm split not in abstract.

endpoint: Change in PROMIS-29 Physical Health Summary Score, baseline to day 28
notes: Adjusted within-arm changes 0.45 (-0.93 to 1.83) vs 1.01 (-0.30 to 2.31); p=0.54. Higher PHSS = better physical health (instrument convention; confirm in full text).

endpoint: Study drug-related treatment-emergent adverse events
notes: 35/46 (76%) vs 27/49 (55%), mostly dysgeusia; no deaths or SAEs to week 6; AE-related early termination 2 vs 1.

endpoint: Change in smartwatch biometric measures (activity, heart rate, SpO2) over 15 weeks, NMV/r vs placebo-ritonavir
population: Wearable substudy: 50 of 94 enrolled met wear-time criteria (37 NMV/r, 13 placebo-ritonavir)
notes: Exploratory substudy; 44/94 excluded for wear-time/completeness (selection). No numeric between-arm estimate extracted.

endpoint: Latent-class PRO trajectory groups; subgroup benefit of NMV/r
notes: PGIS: improving n=17, persistent/severe n=136; PGIC: improving n=130, worsening n=22. Worsening groups had higher proportions of NMV/r-treated participants (descriptive, exploratory; not causal).

endpoint: Fatigue reduction on VAS, IMC-2+NMV/r vs IMC-2 only
units: percent (relative VAS improvement difference as reported)
notes: Non-randomized, unblinded, self-selected groups; p<0.0001 as reported. Not evidence of efficacy of the combination. Brand name in title retained only as bibliographic identity.

endpoint: Side effects reported

source_locators.section: Results: Adverse event and side effect reporting

notes: IO: no side effects reported. IP: increased fatigue 40% and dysgeusia 86.7% during nirmatrelvir/ritonavir course. AUDIT FLAG: 86.7% is not compatible with n=12 IP completers (implies 13/15); denominator not identifiable; ascertainment unsystematic.

endpoint: Within-person change in clinical scales after treatment
notes: Within-group before-after only; no control; patent-holder conflict. Maraviroc is used here as a CCR5 antagonist, not as an anti-SARS-CoV-2 antiviral; indirect to DR018.

endpoint: Fatigue (FAS >22) at 12 weeks
notes: PREVENTION during acute infection, not treatment of established long COVID (DR004 indirect). Per-protocol, 15% not analysed; sample size calculated with 40% power.

endpoint: Any neuropsychiatric post-COVID symptom at 12 weeks
notes: Memory impairment 2/42 vs 5/43 (RR 0.41, 0.08-1.99) and poor concentration 8/42 vs 7/43 (RR 1.17, 0.46-2.93): no significant difference for cognitive items (relevant to DR017, indirect).

endpoint: Time to sustained recovery within 28 days (acute COVID-19)
population: Randomized participants who received study drug (n=2991)
notes: Acute-symptom endpoint, not long COVID. Arm n (1443/1548) differs from pilot study arm n (1439/1544) used in the 6-month report; both kept at result level, not reconciled automatically.

endpoint: Serious adverse events over 180 days
population: Randomized participants who received study drug
notes: Counts only; no comparative estimate reported for SAEs in abstract. Hypoglycemia episodes: 2 metformin vs 4 placebo.

endpoint: Time to sustained recovery
notes: Acute COVID-19 endpoint (not long COVID).

endpoint: Clinical deterioration within 15 days
notes: Acute COVID-19 endpoint. Sign convention as reported by authors (difference at day 15); not re-derived.

endpoint: Emergency-setting observation >6 h or hospitalization due to COVID-19 within 28 days
notes: Acute COVID-19; combination product, effect not attributable to fluvoxamine alone. Proportions 1.8% vs 3.7% (Bayesian).

endpoint: Composite post-acute outcomes (31-300 days), prior metformin vs no metformin
adjustment_set: overlap weighting: demographics, vaccination, comorbidity, prior healthcare utilization
notes: Observational, prevalent-user exposure in T2DM only; association, not causal; not generalizable to non-diabetic people.

endpoint: Post-acute symptoms (31-300 days), prior metformin vs no metformin
notes: Observational; association only.

endpoint: Clinician/patient-reported symptom change after infusion
notes: Uncontrolled case reports; benefit waned in one case; cannot establish efficacy.

endpoint: Adjusted mean change in HbA1c at 24 weeks (per arm)
notes: Indirect for DR014 (formulation question): diabetes population, glycemic endpoint, not long COVID. Adverse events described as similar (no numbers in abstract).

endpoint: Progression-free and overall survival
notes: PFS 2 months; OS 8.5 months; CA-125 fell 303.6 to 54 U/ml at 4 months while lymph nodes increased. No control; not an ivermectin+mebendazole test.

endpoint: Severe hepatocellular liver injury attributed to fenbendazole (RUCAM 8, probable)
timepoint: After dose increase; resolved after stopping
notes: Harm signal; immunotherapy safely reintroduced after stopping fenbendazole.

endpoint: 6-month progression-free survival vs propensity-matched external control
population: Analysed patients vs PS-matched external controls
notes: 88.0% vs 76.9% (p=0.071) PS-matched; unmatched 84.9% vs 72.3%. External control comparison only - not randomized evidence.

endpoint: Change in pain intensity (NRS 0-10) at 3 months
notes: p=0.236, d=0.19; no benefit over placebo. Negative evidence retained.

endpoint: Participants with any adverse event
notes: Mostly mild/transient; no treatment-related serious events.

endpoint: HD:CAS score reduction at week 8, naltrexone vs fluoxetine
notes: Naltrexone not superior to fluoxetine; no placebo arm, so neither drug shown effective vs no treatment. Discontinuation: 6/40 naltrexone; fluoxetine 2 AE withdrawals + 4 discontinued.

endpoint: QIDS-SR reduction at 12 weeks
notes: Not statistically significant (p=0.087; d=-0.72). Hypomania ratings higher at 12 weeks. Bipolar population.

endpoint: Change in SHAPS (anhedonia) at week 9
notes: Single centre; mixed mood disorders; add-on. Not a treatment-resistant-only population.

endpoint: Change in visceral adiposity (DXA) over 48 weeks
notes: eta-p^2=0.001, p=0.942. Adverse and serious adverse events similar across groups. Subgroup gains (lean mass/pain in women on 10 mg) are secondary/exploratory.

endpoint: Change in 30-s chair-stand repetitions at 13 weeks (sirolimus - placebo)
notes: Direction favours placebo; complete-case -2.46 (-4.87 to -0.06) and per-protocol -3.44 (-5.86 to -0.99) significant. Relevant to DR033 exercise-related concern. Arm n 20/20 from 1:1 of 40 per abstract (assignment 1:1).
